payload.title: status=BLOCKED is being used as a CLOCK-based deferral, but nothing ever releases it — the 17:11Z gate on the PaddleOCR critical path has no actuator
payload.not_a_complaint_about_the_gate: PO's freeze is DELIBERATE, documented and correct. Each row carries a gate_note saying so verbatim: 'status=BLOCKED is the market-hours gate, NOT a dependency - blocked_by and depends_on are both empty by design. next_recheck_not_before is the real condition. BLOCKED is used because next_recheck_not_before is currently honoured only by the qa-drain consumer.' The engineering call (do not run the extractor while the AC-7 cgroup-memory series is in flight) is sound. This signal is ONLY about the missing release path.

evidence.actuator_scan: Files mentioning BOTH 'BLOCKED' and 'not_before' across scripts/: exactly 4 — devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq (gate reader, sources review[]/done[]), lib/devteam-eligibility.jq (the predicate itself), test-devteam-donelane-drain.sh (a test), and po-triage-20260826T0536Z-blocked-freeze-and-langvi-ruling.jq (PO's one-shot transform that SET the freeze). None of them scans for BLOCKED rows whose clock has passed and returns them to a live status.
evidence.why_the_one_gate_reader_cannot_help: The four frozen rows sit in task_board.backlog[]. The only picker that honours not-before keys sources review[] UNION done[]. It can never see them. Separately, BLOCKED is excluded from every positive status allowlist, so no backlog picker will touch them either.
evidence.gate_is_well_founded: 17:11:30Z = AC-7 sampler first sample 05:11:30Z + 12h. NOT container start (00:33:39Z) — do not recompute it from the container. Sampler healthy at 33 rows, last sample 07:42:32Z, container restarts=0.
evidence.board_wide_population_NOT_verified: 49 rows board-wide carry status=BLOCKED; only 11 carry any blocked_by. The other 38 were NOT individually inspected — I read only the 4-row batch stamped updated_at=2026-08-26T06:51:41Z. Do NOT treat '38 rows frozen with no blocker' as 38 defects; several may encode a real gate in prose exactly as these four do. Someone must actually read them before any sweep. A bulk unfreeze would be the prose-blind auto-claim failure mode.

payload.impact: The user's standing goal — replace tesseract OCR with Vietnamese PaddleOCR to improve BCTC extraction quality — routes entirely through MEASURE-PDFX-... -> DECIDE-PDFX-.... Both are frozen behind a clock with no reader. Absent manual intervention the goal stalls indefinitely, and the stall is SILENT: the rows look deliberately managed, not stuck.
payload.recommendation: Give the clock an actuator. Either (a) add a backlog-side sweep that returns BLOCKED rows to READY once next_recheck_not_before has passed AND depends_on is satisfied, or (b) stop using BLOCKED for clock deferrals and use a task-lock, which is the only fleet-honored deferral mechanism today. Note this is the THIRD finding of the same shape filed in this tick alone (not-before honored by 1 of 4 pickers, 07:19:50Z; qa[] has no picker, 07:42:56Z; this one) — a guarantee advertised board-wide with zero or one implementing reader. That recurrence is itself worth a root-cause look.
payload.router_action_taken: Armed one-shot session cron 00545d31 for 2026-08-26T17:13Z (local 19:13) to verify the AC-7 window actually closed and then spawn po to release the freeze. NOTE THE WEAKNESS: session crons are in-memory and die with this CLI session, so this actuator does not survive a restart. It is a stopgap, not the fix.
